title: Platform systems & services: how-tos, dashboards, runbooks, retrospective and roadmap
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates platform systems and services guidance: operational how-tos, dashboards and alerting conventions, canonical runbooks, a short retrospective of recent reliability work, and the roadmap for the next two quarters. Target audience: platform engineers, oncall SREs, and service owners.

Scope

- Inventory and ownership for core platform services (see table).
- Standard how-tos for deploying changes, creating dashboards, and authoring alerts.
- Prometheus/Grafana conventions and example alert rules.
- Consolidated runbook templates used during incidents.
- Short retrospective (Q2 2026) and action items.
- Roadmap items (Q3-Q4 2026) and owners.

Service inventory (core)

| Service name | Purpose | Owner | Primary SLOs | Runbook | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| platform-api | Public API gateway for internal services and customer-facing routes | platform-api-team | Availability 99.95% monthly, p95 latency < 200ms | /runbooks/platform-api | Autoscale on queue depth; depends on cluster-manager and kv-cache-service |
| cluster-manager | Orchestration for dedicated GPU pools and routing | infra-scheduling | Availability 99.9%, reconcile latency < 30s | /runbooks/cluster-manager | Critical for Dedicated capacity; strong coupling with cloud accounts |
| metric-ingestor | Central metrics ingestion + tag normalization (Prometheus remote_write endpoint) | observability-team | Data completeness > 99% (5m windows) | /runbooks/metric-ingestor | Backpressure to Kafka on spikes |
| kv-cache-service | Prefix/KV cache used by serving runtime | serving-runtime-team | Cache hit-rate target 85% for interactive workloads | serving-runtime-team | Warmup scripts available in ops repo |
| batch-router | Continuous batching router for token-efficient serving | serving-runtime-team | Throughput SLOs per pool, backpressure < 5% | serving-runtime-team | Streaming and batch variants supported |

How-tos: Deploys and runbook hygiene

1) Release checklist for platform services

- Create a change request in the change-management tracker and link PRs.
- Verify unit + integration tests pass in CI (use the platform-ci job: platform-ci/fast-path).
- Run the canary pipeline: ./scripts/canary-deploy.sh --service SERVICE --env staging.
- Observe staging dashboards for at least 30 minutes. Key checks: error rate, p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization.
- Schedule a 15-minute smoke window for prod rollout. If no regressions, proceed with progressive rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30 minutes.
- Update service runbook ownership in the team wiki if any ownership has changed.

2) Creating a Grafana dashboard (convention)

- Dashboards live in the dashboards repo under dashboards/grafana. Name convention: team-service-main (e.g., serving-runtime-kv-cache-main).
- Panels: health (availability, error rate), latency (p50/p95/p99), resource (cpu/gpu/mem), queueing/backpressure metrics.
- Required variables: env, cluster, region, job.
- Template panel JSON must include: panel.description with links to runbook and recent incidents.
- Submit a PR against dashboards repo and ping observability reviewers.

3) Authoring Prometheus alert rules (best practices)

- Keep alerts actionable and owner-assigned. Every alert must list owner and runbook link in the alert description.
- Use noise-resistant thresholds and duration windows. Prefer rate-based rules when possible.
- Example alert for elevated 5m error rate:

- alert: PlatformApiHighErrorRate
  expr: increase(platform_api_request_errors_total[5m]) / increase(platform_api_requests_total[5m]) > 0.05
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: High error rate on platform-api (>5% over 10m)
    runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-api
    owner: platform-api-team

- Example GPU utilization alert for cluster-manager nodes:

- alert: GPUHighUtilization
  expr: avg_over_time(nvidia_gpu_utilization_percent[10m]) > 85
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: GPU utilization > 85% for 15m in cluster-manager pool
    runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/cluster-manager
    owner: infra-scheduling

Dashboards and alerts: conventions and ownership

- Dashboards are assigned to teams; owners respond to dashboard regressions during business hours.
- Alerts labeled severity: page, high, medium, info. page -> immediate pager; high -> oncall Slack channel; medium -> ticket to triage.
- Alert fatigue mitigation: if an alert pages more than 3 times in 24h, flag it for rule tuning and schedule a short investigation.

Platform runbook template (canonical)

- Title: incident short summary
- Impact: services affected, customer impact, user-facing symptoms
- Detection: how it was detected (alert id, dashboard, customer report)
- Initial triage (first 15 minutes):
  1. Acknowledge alert and pull scribe.
  2. Determine blast radius: which clusters/pools/regions are impacted.
  3. Identify recent changes (deploys, infra changes) in last 60 minutes.
  4. If paging, assign remediation owner and mitigation owner.
- Mitigation steps (ordered): list specific commands and safe rollbacks. Example commands:
  - Check service health: kubectl -n platform get pods -o wide | egrep SERVICE_NAME
  - Check logs: stern -n platform SERVICE_NAME --since 1h
  - Restart pod (safe path): kubectl -n platform rollout restart deployment/SERVICE_NAME
- Escalation matrix: page service owner -> platform lead -> oncall manager (include contact rotations in team wiki).
- Communication: update incident channel, status page, and record timeline.
- Post-incident: create a postmortem within 72 hours and link to runbook.

Retrospective: Q2 2026 (summary)

- Summary: Q2 saw two high-severity incidents affecting Dedicated capacity routing and one regression causing elevated request tail latency on platform-api. Root causes: incomplete rollout gating for a routing change and a client-side backpressure regression.
- Key outcomes:
  - Implemented canary traffic shaping in cluster-manager (10% increments with automatic rollback).
  - Added a p99 latency guardrail to CI smoke tests for platform-api PRs.
  - Created a dedicated dashboard for batch-router backpressure metrics.
- Action items (status):
  - A1: Expand smoke test coverage to include synthetic prefix-cache warmups (owner: serving-runtime-team) - in progress.
  - A2: Tune alert thresholds for metric-ingestor to reduce noisy pages (owner: observability-team) - done.
  - A3: Improve incident telemetry to include recent deploy ids in all primary dashboards (owner: eng-platform) - in progress.

Roadmap: Q3-Q4 2026 (high-level initiatives)

- Q3 2026 (owner: eng-platform)
  - Initiative: Unified incident playbooks and automated postmortem scaffolding. Deliverable: templated postmortem form, auto-populate timeline from pagerduty and slack.
  - Initiative: Dashboard ownership migration to team-specific folders and automated dashboard linting in CI.
  - Initiative: Rollout of GPU predictive scaling (pilot with Dedicated beta customers). Owner: infra-scheduling.

- Q4 2026 (owner: serving-runtime + observability)
  - Initiative: KV cache warm start improvements and pre-warming orchestration. Goal: improve cache hit-rate by 5% on cold start.
  - Initiative: Observability 2.0: metric cardinality controls and improved tagging standards.

Team wiki and ongoing maintenance

- Every team must appoint a dashboard owner and update the wiki page quarterly. The eng-platform team will run an audit of dashboard ownership in October 2026.
- Runbook reviews must be scheduled at least once per quarter. Ensure runbooks include verification commands, mitigation steps, and ownership.
- Documentation conventions: use confluence-style headings, short intro, bulleted and numbered procedures, and clearly labeled escalation steps. Link related pages and include runbook IDs in alert annotations.

Appendices

A: Common commands
- kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=SERVICE -o wide
- stern -n platform SERVICE --since 1h | pv -qL 1000
- ./scripts/canary-deploy.sh --service SERVICE --env staging

B: Example alert rule (Prometheus recording rule)
- groups:
  - name: platform.rules
    rules:
      - record: job:platform_api_error_rate:5m
        expr: increase(platform_api_request_errors_total[5m]) / increase(platform_api_requests_total[5m])

C: Contacts and rotations
- Oncall rotations live in the eng-platform rota doc. For urgent paging: platform-oncall@company.internal (pagerduty mapping in rota doc).

If you have edits or suggestions, please open a PR against this document or ping the eng-platform channel.
